headline: Bitcoin Falls 5.10% to $55,830
deck: CoinDesk put the quarterly decline at 28% and reported $2.40 billion in crypto-futures liquidations over the preceding 24 hours.
body: Bitcoin fell 5.10% to $55,830 by 11:13 p.m. Eastern time on Friday, its lowest level since September 2024, Tasnim reported. Reuters also reported the price and decline. [E1][E2]
Reuters reported that Bitcoin had earlier fallen below $60,000 for the first time since July. [E3]
Reuters reported that the decline came amid trading that weighed on other risk assets. [E4]
CoinDesk said the sell-off deepened a bear market that began after Bitcoin peaked above $126,000 in October last year, and that Bitcoin was down 28% for the quarter. [E5][E6]
CoinDesk cited Coinglass data showing $2.40 billion in crypto-futures liquidations over the preceding 24 hours. [E8]

Cointelegraph reported that Bitcoin's earlier drop below $60,000 came amid a broader sell-off in technology stocks and other risk assets, and put the cryptocurrency's losses at 13.8% over the week and nearly 30% over the month. [E9][E10]

CoinDesk reported that analysts pointed to rising inflation-adjusted U.S. Treasury yields as a key driver. James Butterfill, CoinShares' head of research, told Cointelegraph that the decline appeared to reflect the broader sell-off in artificial-intelligence stocks more than problems specific to cryptocurrency markets. [E7][E11]
